title: Rutgers men’s basketball coach Steve Pikiell announces he has cancer
content:
Rutgers men’s basketball coach Steve Pikiell had successful surgery following a cancer diagnosis, but ongoing treatment will force him to take leave from his full-time duties, he disclosed in a letter to Rutgers supporters Wednesday.

Associate head coach Brandin Knight will guide the team while Pikiell recovers.

After “not feeling 100 percent” a few months ago, Pikiell said, he visited a team of doctors for tests, and an undisclosed form of cancer was discovered. Pikiell said he and his doctors “have a kick-ass game plan to finish treatment.”

“I will still be involved with the team to the best of my ability as I navigate the challenges of the season through treatment,” Pikiell said. “I have great confidence in Coach Knight, the rest of the talented staff, and our exceptional student-athletes. I know they will do an amazing job leading our program when I’m not able to.”

Pikiell, 58, enters his 11th season at Rutgers, and his 161 wins are third-most in program history. He also has Rutgers’ most victories against ranked opponents (17) and directed two teams to the NCAA tournament, plus a third that was likely to qualify for the canceled 2020 postseason. Pikiell played collegiately at UConn under Jim Calhoun and coached Stony Brook for 11 years.
